JOSE NETU M. TAMAYO HON. JESLITO C. SEEN MAYBELYN ROSE DC. FERNANDEZ ALVIN T. COQUIA DENNIS C. CANTO MARVIN V. FABIA MARCELINO D. FERNANDEZ Sangguniang Panlungsod Members Dagupan City Gentlemen and Lady: 'I'his has reiérence to your letter dated IO July 2017 requesting the Department's legal opinion on several issues in connection with your plan to transfer the City l•lall to a new site. Per your letter, the City Govermnent of Dagupan is planning to construct a new City Hall on a land to be donated by Mr. Kerwin Fernandez, the brother of Dagupan City Mayor Belen Fernandez. Surrounding the parcels of land to be donated are as follows: l. On the north side, Mr. Matias and CSI Corporation properties; 2. On the west is a creek; 3. On the south is owned by CSI (measuring 16, 229 square meters) and Dagupan City Mayor Belen Fernandez (measuring 6,000 square meters); and 4. On the east bounded by Lot No. 2957-2, owned by CSI. Per your letter, while the donor is not the mayor but her brother, still legal questions raised by opponents of the project that the increase in the value of the properties of CSI and Mayor Fernandez is tantamount to violation of Republic Act No. 3019 due to alleged conflict of interest on account of benefit that will arise from the development of the project. For this, you are asking the Department's legal opinion on the following issues:

l. Should the Sanggunian Illembersapprove the ordinance transférring the City Ila]] to [he parcel of land donated by Kerwin Fernandez, brother of Mayor Belen Fernandez, will the members thereof be held liable for anti-graft on account of the alleged conflict of interest on the part of the mayor by reason OT Ihe increased value of the surrounding land? Otherwise put, will the members thereof voting in favor of the transfer be liable for violation of Republic Act No. 3019 and Republic Act No. 6713 on account of incidental benefits derived by CSI Group of Companies, a corporation to which the mayor is a shareholder of the corporation the lands adjoining thereto? '2. Will the mayor be held for anti-graft and corrupt practices under RA 3019 on account of the perceived increase in value of the adjoining parcels of land by reason of development of adjoining properties as stockholder of' CSI and • as owner ofa portion of parcel of lands therein (sic)? You also represented in your letter that although the CSI and Mayor Fernandez are owners of the adjoining properties, several owners will likewise benefit from the development Of the area by reason of introduction of the proposed City Hall pursuant to the Dagupan City Comprehensive Land Use Plan duly approved by the Housing and Land Use Regulatory Board (HLURB). At the outset, we deem it prudent to define the term "conflict of interest", thus: a. Section 51 (a) of Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 "Conflict of interest" refers in general to one where it may be reasonably deduced that a member of a sanggunian may not act in the public interest due to some private, pecuniary, or other personal considerations that may tend to affect his judgment to the prejudice of the service or the public. b. Section 3 (i) of Republic Act No. 6713 or the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees "Conflict of interest" arises when a public official or employee is a member of a board, an officer, or a substantial stockholder of a private corporation or owner or has a substantial interest in a business, and the interest of such corporation or business, or his rights or duties therein, may be opposed to or affected by the [Ilithful performance of official duty. In relation thereto, Section 9 of RA 6713 enumerates acts which constitute prohibited acts and transactions: SECTION 7. Prohibited Acts and addition to acts and omissions of' public officials and employees now prescribed in the

Constitution and existing Ia vvs, the follovving shall constitute prohibitecracts and transactions of any public official and employee and are hereby declared to be unlavvful: (a) Financial and material interest. —Public officials and employees shall not, directly or indirectly, have any financial or material interest in any transaction requiring the approval of their office. (b) Outside employment and other activities related thereto. —Public officials and employees during their incumbency shall not: (I) Own, control, manage or accept employment as officer, employee, consultant, counsel, broker, agent, trustee or nominee in any private enterprise regulated, supervised or licensed by their office unless expressly allowed by law; " Also, worthy of note is Section 3(h) and (i) of RA 3019 or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, thus: SECTION 3. Corrupt practices of' public officers.—ln addition to acts or omissions of public officers already penalized by existing law, the following shall constitute corrupt practices of any public officer and are hereby declared to be unlawful: (e) Causing any undue injury to any party, including the Government, or giving any private party any unwarranted benefits, advantage or preference in the discharge of his official administrative or judicial functions through manifOst partiality, evident bad faith or gross inexcusable negligence. This provision shall apply to officers and employees of offices or government corporations charged with the grant of licenses or permits or other concessions. Entering, on behalf of the Government, into any contract or transaction manifestly and grossly disadvantageous to the same, whether or not the public oflicer profited or will profit thereby. (h) Directly or indirectly having financial or pecuniary interest in any business, contract or transaction in connection with which he intervenes or takes part in his official capacity, or in which he is prohibited by Lhe Constitution or by any law from having any interest. Directly or indirectly becoming interested, for personal gain, or having a material interest in any transaction or act requiring the approval of a board, panel or group of which he is a member, and which exercises

discretion in such approval, even if he votes against the same or does not participate in tho action Of the board, committee, panel or group. Interest för personal gain shall be presumed against those public officers responsible for the approval of manifestly unlawful, inequitable, or irregular transactions or acts by the board, panel or group to which they belong. xxx Based on the foregoing, conflict of interest arises whenever a public official or employee, by faithfully performing his official duty, may oppose or affect the interest of a private corporation or business to which he is also affiliated, either as a member Of a board, olTicer or a substantial stockholder. Accordingly, if the faithful performance of his official duty will oppose or affect the interest of a private corporation or business to which he is affiliated, there is no conflict of interest to speak of'. Thus, we can aptly say that conflict of interest does not ipso facto arise whenever a public official or employee holds another position in a private corporation or business. 'I'he rationale behind the prohibition on conflict of interest is that no public officer shall be permitted to entertain two (2) conflicting loyalties one, public, and' the other, private, with regard to matters brought befbre his consideration. Experiences consistently tell us that where private interest clashes with the duty to uphold public interest, the tendency is that the concerned public officer will favor his personal interest. The test of conflict of interest therefore is whether the activity, investment, relationship or interest involving the private corporation or business to which a public official or employee is affiliated may prevent him from faithlillly discharging his duty as such public official or employee. Otherwise, there arises no conflict of interest. Going now to your first query, we are of the view that the Sangguniang Panlungsod Members who will sign the ordinance transferring the City Hall to the parcel of land to be donated by the brother of MQyor Fernandez are not liable for anti-graft and corrupt practices quoted above for the following reasons: a) Conflict of interest as defined under RA 6713 and the corrupt practices mentioned in paragraphs (h) and (i) of RA 3019 presuppose that the public official in faithlillly performing an official duty will oppose or affect his own interest in a private corporation or business to which he is affiliated. In the case at hand, it appears that there is no Sangguniang Panlungsod Mem ber who has financial or pecuniary interest in the CSI Group of Companies, the corporation that is perceived to be benefited by the donation. It is rather Mayor Belen Fernandez who is a shareholder therein; b) Mr. Kerwin Fernandez is the only one in Dagupan City who is offering to donate a property as the new site of the City Hall. Hence, in enacting the aforesaid

discretion in such approval, even if he votes against the same or does not participate in the action Of the board, committee, panel or group. Going now to your first query, we are of the view that the Sangguniang Panlungsod Members who will sign the ordinance transferring the City Hall to the parcel of' land to be donated by the brother of IVIqyor Fernandez are not liable for anti-graft and corrupt practices quoted above for the following reasons: a) Conflict of interest as defined under RA 6713 and the corrupt practices mentioned in paragraphs (h) and (i) of RA 3019 presuppose that the public official in faithfillly performing an official duty will oppose or afTéct his own interest in a private corporation or business to which he is affiliated. In the case at hand, it appears that there is no Sangguniang Panlungsod Member who has financial or pecuniary interest in the CSI Group of Companies, the corporation that is perceived to be benefited by the donation. It is rather Mayor Belen Fernandez who is a shareholder therein; b) Mr. Kerwin Fernandez is the only one in Dagupan City who is offering to donate a property as the new site of the City Hall. Hence, in enacting the aforesaid

ordinance, the members of the Sangguniang Panlungsod cannot be said to have given unwarranted benefits, advantage or preference mentioned in paragraph (e) of RA 3019 in favor of Mr. Kerwin Fernandez; c) Since it is a donation, the Sangguniang Panlungsod Members cannot also be said to be entering a contract or transaction manifestly and grossly disadvantageous to the government mentioned in paragraph (g) of RA 3019. With regard to your second query, we also reply in the negative. While it is true that Mayor Belen Fernandez is the one who shall be accepting the donation being the local chief executive of Dagupan City, in doing so, she is merely acting pursuant to the ordinance enacted by the Sangguniang Panlungsod. Section 455 (b)(2) of the Local Government Code of 1991 mandates the City Mayor to enforce all ordinances relative to the governance of the city. Moreover, we are of the view that the corresponding increase in value of the parcels 01' land adjoining the donated property is only incidental. In fact, per your representation, it is not only the CSI Group of Companies and Mayor Fernandez who will be benefited by such increase in value of the properties therein but also other owners of properties adjoining the area. We hope to have guided you accordingly. e truly yours, AU ERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary Ls:'17 Copy furnished: DIRECIOR JAMI'S F.
